description: The STIMULUS half of the claim-identity falsification loop (#5041, ADR-0037 §9). Human-authored, synthetic, in-repo — the repo is public, so real customer chat cannot be the source. Each entry is a PAIR of messages plus a claim about what they MEAN relative to each other. It contains no subject, predicate or object anyone chose: those are produced by driving the real extractor over these messages (`bun packages/cli/bin/brain-paraphrase-eval.ts`) and recorded in `extracted.json`, which is what the deterministic suite consumes. A corpus whose predicate side is hand-authored is the fixture-that-agrees-by-construction trap in a file with a better name.

rubric.what_a_human_may_write_here: The message bodies, and `relation` — a statement about English, which a human is the right oracle for. Never a triple, never a key, never a verdict.
rubric.how_it_is_graded: The eval drives the real extractor over every message and compares the emitted triples against `extracted.json` byte for byte. Any difference is DRIFT and fails the run; the fix is to regenerate the artifact as a reviewed commit (`--write`), never to loosen the comparison. FOUR corpus-honesty checks ride along, and any one of them failing means the corpus has stopped exercising what it claims to: a `no-claim` pair that produces a triple; any other pair that produces none on a side; any pair producing MORE THAN ONE claim a side (the deterministic suite reads exactly one and throws otherwise, so the two ends would hold different contracts); and any claim carrying a slot that normalizes away, since a blank surface keys to null and every prohibition downstream would pass without the identity layer doing anything. The loader additionally refuses a corpus that is all `no-claim` (a dead extractor would grade honest) or has no `no-claim` control at all.
rubric.why_pairs_and_not_items: Identity is a relation between two claims. A single message can only ever demonstrate extraction; it takes two to demonstrate that two spellings of one belief do — or do not — land in one slot.

pairs.why: ⭐ #5000's own shape, reached the way the bug reached production: two people state one price in a working week and nobody phrases it twice the same. Both messages assert one fact about one product at one price, so a reader would call them one claim. Whether the extractor spells the relationship with a copula on one side and without it on the other is exactly what this corpus refuses to assume — it is the recorded answer, not the input. The subject and the amount are held steady in the PROSE so that whatever varies in the recording varies because the extractor varied it.

a.body: Confirming for the pricing deck: the Business tier is priced at $499 a month.

b.body: For the FAQ — we price the Business tier at $499 a month.

pairs.why: The reporting line, stated as a verb on one side and as a noun on the other, WITHOUT swapping who is who — Ada is the subject of both sentences and Grace the value of both. That separation is the whole point of keeping this entry apart from `leads-inverse` below: here a collapse is correct and an over-match costs nothing, there a collapse retires a true belief. A corpus with only one of the two cannot tell a rule that helps from a rule that harms.

a.body: Heads up: Ada reports to Grace as of this sprint.

b.body: For the org chart — Ada's manager is Grace.

pairs.why: A recurring window, stated twice. Deliberately not a price and not a person: if every `same-claim` entry in the corpus were about money, a drift in the recording could not be told apart from a drift in how the extractor handles money in particular. The object here is a weekday, which parses to no comparable value at all — so the pair reaches the identity layer through the KEY arm alone.

a.body: The deploy job runs on Thursdays.

b.body: Scheduling note: the deploy job is scheduled for Thursdays.

pairs.why: One amount, two ways of writing money — the `499 USD` / `USD 499` shape that ADR-0037 §2 pins, arriving from prose rather than from a fixture. This is the entry whose interesting axis is the OBJECT: the two messages are as close as English allows on subject and relationship, so a difference in the recorded object surface is the extractor's, not the sentence's. It is what gives the deterministic suite a pair that can only corroborate through a comparable VALUE if it corroborates at all.

⭐ THE live #5000 instance, and the reason ADR-0037 §6 corrects T4's worked example. The prod rows were `499 a month` and `599 a month`: the objects DISAGREE, so this is a contradiction and not a restatement, and the alias proposer returns zero candidates for it BY DESIGN. It is here as the shape the identity layer must reach a DIFFERENT verdict on from every `same-claim` entry above — without it, a recording where everything collides and a recording where nothing does are equally green.

a.body: Confirming for the pricing deck: the Business tier is priced at $499 a month.

b.body: Update — we now charge $599 a month for the Business tier.

pairs.why: ⭐ THE positive control for the abstain band, and it exists because the corpus without it could not tell *abstained* from *broken*. `price-contradiction` above is the shape the bug reported, and both of its amounts are written the way people write them in chat — `$499 a month`, three tokens, which the money grammar refuses. So every comparable value in this corpus would be NULL, agreement would be `unknown` everywhere, and a value parser that had stopped working entirely would look identical to one abstaining correctly. Here both amounts carry an explicit ISO-4217 code, so both sides are comparable AS MONEY and their difference is positive evidence rather than two strings failing to match. Same contradiction, stated in the register a pricing page uses rather than the one a Slack thread does.

b.body: Correction — Starter is priced at 599 USD.

pairs.why: ⚠️ `led_by` and `leads` — INVERSE relations, live in the corpus that started this map, and the pair every lexical near-miss detector ranks at the top. One fact stated from both ends: the subject of each sentence is the object of the other. Collapsing them is not an over-match on a synonym, it is an assertion that a claim and its converse occupy one slot, which at `single` cardinality hands the publish gate a `valid_to` stamp on a true belief. This entry exists so that a rule which passes every `same-claim` pair above still has to survive the one place where collapsing is destructive.

b.body: Just so it's written down: the Osprey rollout is led by Ana.

pairs.why: What a tier costs and what it costs to RENEW are different questions, and both answers are true at once. The two messages share a subject and an amount-shaped object, so nothing but the relationship holds them apart — which is what makes this the predicate arm's falsifier at the message level. A normalization rule loose enough to fold `priced at` into `renews at` would have both beliefs in one slot and one of them retired.

a.body: The Business tier is priced at $499 a month.

b.body: The Business tier renews at $449 a month.

pairs.why: Two tiers, each with its own price — no contradiction, nothing to arbitrate. The relationship and the shape of the object are as close as the corpus gets, so the SUBJECT is the only thing keeping these apart, and a subject arm that stopped discriminating would show up here and nowhere else.

a.body: The Business tier is priced at $499 a month.

b.body: The Starter tier is priced at $199 a month.

pairs.why: ⭐ THE positive control for the extractor itself, and the entry that keeps every prohibition in this corpus honest. An empty list is the correct answer for greetings and status noise — and an extractor that had silently stopped working returns an empty list for EVERYTHING, which would satisfy every `different-claim` entry above while proving nothing. Grading it in the other direction (this pair must produce nothing, every other pair must produce something) is what separates a discriminating extractor from a broken one.

a.body: morning all — coffee machine is fixed 🎉

b.body: anyone else seeing that flaky test on main, or just me?
